developments: The Nasdaq fell about 4% at the US open after hotter-than-expected core PCE inflation, new US tariff proposals and fresh doubts over AI spending, Bitcoin Magazine reported.
Bitcoin dropped to about $57,210 on Kraken shortly after the open, then recovered to near $58,540 by 16:30 UK.
ZEC fell about 6.5% since this morning to near $688, its first big drop of the week.
briefing.changed: Clearly weaker than this morning. The inflation data came in hot, stocks sold off hard, and bitcoin briefly broke below the $58,500 level flagged on Tuesday before bouncing back to it. ZEC stopped holding up and fell further than bitcoin.
briefing.question: Can bitcoin hold above its weekend low near $55,100 if US stocks keep falling into the Thanksgiving break?
briefing.watch: Wednesday's US close at 21:00 UK and the day's ETF flows this evening. The next 🔴 event is the Fed decision on Wednesday 9 December at 19:00 UK.

lead.headline: Hot inflation and tariff threat sink Nasdaq 4%, dragging bitcoin lower
lead.standfirst: A firmer-than-expected US inflation reading and new tariff proposals hit technology shares at the open, and bitcoin briefly fell to about $57,200 before steadying.
body: The Nasdaq Composite fell about 4% early in Wednesday's US session, with the S&P 500 down about 3%, Bitcoin Magazine reported. Nvidia sank more than 8%, and Micron and AMD each fell more than 9%.

The selling followed October's PCE figures, the Fed's preferred inflation gauge. Core PCE rose to 3.3% a year, above the 3.2% forecast, while headline PCE was 3.8%, CNBC and Bitcoin Magazine reported. Third-quarter growth was revised up to 4.3%.

Separately, the US proposed new tariffs on 14 trading partners including China, the EU and Japan, Euronews reported. The UK is not on the list, and a comment period could delay any duties until January.

Bitcoin fell to about $57,210 on Kraken shortly after the open, below the $58,500 level Glassnode had flagged, before recovering to near $58,540 by 16:30 UK. Zcash fell harder, with ZEC down about 6.5% since the morning to near $688.
Fund selling continued. US spot bitcoin ETFs lost $231.6 million on Tuesday, according to SoSoValue data reported by Cointelegraph, taking November's outflows to a record $4.94 billion.
Markets already price a near-certain Fed rate rise on 9 December, Bitcoin Magazine reported, and US markets close on Thursday for Thanksgiving.

headline: Hot core inflation and new US tariff proposals sent the Nasdaq down about 4%, and bitcoin briefly fell to $57,200 before steadying near $58,500. ZEC dropped about 6.5%.
spoken: Cryptonaire Post, afternoon edition. US inflation came in a little hotter than expected, and with new tariff proposals and worries about AI spending, the Nasdaq fell about four per cent at the open. Bitcoin dropped to around fifty-seven thousand, two hundred dollars, then bounced back to about fifty-eight thousand, five hundred. Zcash fell about six and a half per cent to around six hundred and ninety dollars. Bitcoin funds have now lost a record four point nine billion dollars this month. The UK is not on the new tariff list. The next red event is the Fed decision on the ninth of December at seven in the evening. Information only, not advice.

stories.title: Hot core PCE and AI doubts send the Nasdaq down about 4%
stories.why: Core PCE rose to 3.3% a year in October against a 3.2% forecast, with headline at 3.8% and Q3 growth revised to 4.3%, CNBC and Bitcoin Magazine reported. The Nasdaq fell about 4% early on, Nvidia more than 8%. Bitcoin has been trading closely with tech shares, so this was the day's main driver.

note.read: A firmer inflation print hardens the case for a December rate rise and further hikes, which weighs on both tech and crypto.
note.alt: Thin pre-holiday trading and trend-following funds may be exaggerating the move; the data was only slightly above forecast.
note.change: A strong rebound in tech into the US close would suggest the selling was positioning rather than a new leg down.

stories.title: Bitcoin briefly breaks $58,500, touching $57,200, then steadies
stories.why: Kraken showed a low near $57,210 shortly after the US open and bitcoin back near $58,540 at 16:30 UK, down about $430 since this morning. The new evidence is that the $58,500 level flagged on Tuesday gave way intraday but price recovered to it; the weekend low near $55,100 was the lowest in over two years, Bitcoin Magazine reported.

note.read: The quick bounce suggests buyers are still active below $58,000, even with stocks sharply lower.
note.alt: The bounce may simply be short covering in thin trade, with the trend still pointing down.
note.change: A daily close below $58,500 would matter more than an intraday dip; a fall towards $55,100 would mean a retest of the weekend low.

stories.title: US proposes new tariffs on 14 trading partners; UK not included
stories.why: The US trade representative proposed Section 301 tariffs on 14 economies including China, the EU, Japan, South Korea and Taiwan, Euronews and CNBC reported; some Chinese goods would face an extra 20%. The UK is not on the list. A comment period could delay duties until January, but the news added to the risk-off mood.

note.read: Tariff threats feed inflation worries just as the Fed is set to raise rates, a poor mix for risk assets.
note.alt: As a proposal with a comment period, it may be a negotiating tool that is softened before it takes effect.
note.change: Firm start dates or retaliation from China or the EU would raise the stakes.

stories.title: ETF outflows set a monthly record at $4.94 billion
stories.why: US spot bitcoin ETFs lost $231.6 million on Tuesday, their sixth straight day of outflows, according to SoSoValue data reported by Cointelegraph. November's $4.94 billion now beats June's record of $4.51 billion. This morning's edition gave Tuesday as $570 million; see corrections.
stories.caveat: Farside's figure for Tuesday, as cited by CoinDesk, was very close at $231.4 million.

stories.title: ZEC drops about 6.5% to near $688
stories.why: Kraken showed ZEC near $688 at 16:30 UK, down from about $736 this morning, after a low near $673. This morning ZEC was holding up better than bitcoin; this afternoon it fell further. No Zcash-specific news was found to explain it, so it looks like the wider sell-off.

stories.title: More bitcoin holders trim: NXTT sells 500 BTC, Ark sells some of its own ETF
stories.why: Next Technology Holding sold about 500 BTC for $29.2 million and said it does not expect to buy more, an SEC filing reported by Bitcoin Magazine showed. Ark sold $6.8 million of its ARKB fund on Tuesday, The Block reported. Small amounts, but they fit this week's pattern after CleanSpark's plans.

stories.title: Stablecoin redemptions of $12 billion point to money leaving crypto
stories.why: Net redemptions across 11 stablecoins were about $12 billion in the 30 days to 13 November, Kaiko data reported by Cointelegraph showed, the biggest cash-out since 2022. Kaiko said it looked like capital leaving crypto rather than moving within it, though supply has been almost flat since 13 November.

explained.title: Headline versus core inflation
body: Headline inflation counts everything people buy. Core inflation leaves out food and energy, which swing about with weather and oil prices, so it gives a steadier view of the underlying trend.
Central banks such as the Fed watch core most closely. That is why a core reading just a tenth of a point above forecast, as today, can move markets more than the headline number.

investigating: Do Wednesday's ETF flows show the outflow streak continuing? Evidence: Farside or SoSoValue data this evening.
Is ZEC's drop only the wider sell-off, or is there Zcash-specific selling? Evidence: Zcash news, exchange announcements, or ZEC moving differently from bitcoin overnight.
corrections: This morning's edition said US spot bitcoin ETFs lost $570 million on Tuesday, citing The Block. SoSoValue and Farside data, as reported by Cointelegraph, put Tuesday's outflow at about $231.5 million.
